title: Token exchange with a third-party actor token: accepted
lede: {{castApp}} exchanges a PingOne user token plus a {{vendorName}} token. All checks pass, so PingOne reads the resource attribute mapping and issues a token. Mock only. The order of checks is UNVERIFIED.

steps.title: Subject token from PingOne
steps.what: {{castApp}} signs the user in at PingOne (authorization code flow) and holds a PingOne access token: the subject token.

steps.title: Ask the issuer for a token
steps.what: {{castApp}} also gets a token from {{vendorName}}. This is the actor token. It is signed by that issuer, not by PingOne.

steps.title: Third-party JWT comes back
steps.what: The actor token, shown decoded. State: {{stateLabel}}.

steps.title: Token exchange request
steps.what: {{castApp}} sends the RFC 8693 exchange with actor_token_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt. The request shape was MEASURED live against PingOne on 2026-10-27 (the guide shows it only as an image).

steps.title: PingOne asks for the issuer keys
steps.what: PingOne fetches the trusted issuer's JWKS to verify the actor token's signature. The order of checks here is ours (UNVERIFIED).
steps.why:
GET <JWKS URL of the trusted issuer>
keys for {{vendorIssuer}}

steps.title: Issuer keys
steps.what: The JWKS answers. PingOne now runs its checks: assignment, issuer, signature, exp, iat, nbf, audience.

steps.title: All checks pass, read the mapping
steps.what: Every check passed. PingOne reads the attribute mapping on the custom resource {{castResource}}.

steps.title: Mapping expressions
steps.what: The mapping reads claims from the actor token: {{mappingSummary}}

steps.title: Access token issued
steps.what: PingOne issues an access token for the resource with the mapped claims. MOCK token, never verifiable.
